on_screen_text.text: It's not wrong to be different.
Equality begins when we open up and embrace all of our differences.
We hope today is one step forward to respecting and understanding each and every one as a valuable person.

spoken_summary: Members of the K-pop group BTS speak in Korean at the White House. The first speaker, Suga, says, "It's not wrong to be different. Equality begins when we open up and embrace all of our differences." The second speaker, V, adds, "Everyone has their own history. We hope today is one step forward to respecting and understanding each and every one as a valuable person."
audio_music: The audio consists entirely of speech in Korean, with the ambient sound of camera shutters clicking in the background. There is no music. The tone is formal and serious.
editing_pacing: The editing consists of static shots of the speakers at the podium, with simple cuts between the two main speakers. The pacing is slow and consistent with a press conference clip.
central_claim: The globally influential K-pop group BTS visited the White House to advocate for equality, respect, and the acceptance of individual differences.
intended_effect: To create a positive association between the Democratic party and the popular group BTS, and to promote a message of inclusion and unity.
